title: The five-cycle Swift count test of ASASSN-14ko decay depends on its 2024 dip
abstract: We test the ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock directly with 55 Swift photon-count observations in five cycles. Each cycle has a free dip amplitude, residual floor and transition width. A constant midpoint clock gains 23.28 in twice log likelihood over the published local decay. A normal-CDF shape, wider width bounds and daily binning retain gains of 21.11 to 23.49. Removing the 2024 dip reduces the gain to 0.43. Thus the earlier four cycles alone do not separate the two clocks under this model. We supply a count simulation calibration and event-removal tests. The result depends on a smooth monotone ingress family, selected clean cycles and independent negative-binomial count variation. It does not identify the stellar orbital clock or explain the period stall. Code, source hashes, aggregate fits and a separate-scratch retrieval recipe are included.

citations.reason: Verified Swift source counts and original constant dip clock.
Independent NICER markers and wandering dip onsets.
Exact interval test motivates count-level inference.
Recovery clock uses different windows and fixed ingresses.
Independent late X-ray event is outside this Swift-only test.
